nodes.name: Tall elephant grasses
nodes.desc: Tall grasses cover the largest share of the park, and regrow quickly after the monsoon floods and winter burns that open new feeding ground.

nodes.name: Bermuda grass
nodes.desc: A short creeping grass that Wikipedia lists among the main foods of the Indian rhinoceros and the wild water buffalo.

nodes.name: Aquatic plants
nodes.desc: Floating and submerged plants of the beels, or flood lakes. Rhinos eat them, but invasive water hyacinth can choke the water bodies.

nodes.name: Elephant apple
nodes.desc: A fruiting tree of the open woodland. A GloBI record shows Asian elephants eating it.

nodes.name: Indian rhinoceros
nodes.desc: A grazer of grasses that also eats leaves, fruit and aquatic plants. Over 70% of the species lives at Kaziranga, and tigers sometimes take unguarded calves.

nodes.name: Wild water buffalo
nodes.desc: Grazes grasses and sedges in wet grasslands and swamps. Adults are preyed on by tigers.

nodes.name: Asian elephant
nodes.desc: Eats grasses and fruit, with GloBI records for elephant apple. Tigers have been recorded taking calves.

nodes.name: Swamp deer
nodes.desc: A deer of the wet grassland, one of the species tigers hunt in the park.

nodes.name: Hog deer
nodes.desc: The most recorded deer near the park. It lives in the tall grass and is taken by tigers, jungle cats and pythons in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots for plant foods in the grassland and woodland, and is itself prey for tigers.

nodes.name: Freshwater fish
nodes.desc: About 42 fish species live in the area. Many graze plants and small animals of the rivers and beels, and feed otters, eagles and storks.

nodes.name: Greater adjutant
nodes.desc: A stork that mostly eats carrion and offal but also catches fish and frogs. Kaziranga once held the only known breeding site.

nodes.name: Grey-headed fish eagle
nodes.desc: A raptor of the park wetlands that Wikipedia lists among its fish-eating birds.

nodes.name: Smooth-coated otter
nodes.desc: A fish-eating otter of the Brahmaputra channels and beels, itself recorded as tiger prey.

nodes.name: Jungle cat
nodes.desc: A small wild cat of wet grassland and scrub that hunts deer fawns, rodents and birds.

nodes.name: Indian rock python
nodes.desc: A large constrictor that GloBI records eating hog deer.

nodes.name: Bengal tiger
nodes.desc: The top predator. It hunts deer, wild boar and buffalo, and rarely takes young elephants or rhinos.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm sunny months drive fast regrowth of the grasses.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: June to September rains bring most of the year's water to the park.

nodes.name: Brahmaputra floods
nodes.desc: Floods can cover most of the park for days, drive animals to higher ground and leave fresh silt and new grass behind.

nodes.name: Winter burning
nodes.desc: Park staff burn tall grass in winter, and animals gather on the burnt patches to eat new shoots.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass and carcasses and return nutrients to the floodplain soil.
